NOW ARRIVING: Asteroid Field 1! Trip cost: −4 FOOD, −3 H2O, −2 FUEL, +1 MORALE, −1 O2, 10 DAYS. RATE your journey!

You signed. RESULTS: +5 MORALE, 1 DAY! ★★★★★

expand.title: THE BEACON'S PLATE
expand.text:
Riveted to the beacon's housing, a plate: the names of the crew who set it, the year, and a line somebody scratched in later — 'Like the old Voyager. Still talking.'

Voyager 1 left Earth in 1977 on a tour of the outer planets and never stopped. In 2012 it crossed out of the Sun's bubble of wind into interstellar space, the first thing people ever built to do it. Its radio runs on roughly the power of a refrigerator bulb, and its signal takes the better part of a day to get home. Home is still listening.

It carries a golden record of greetings, music and the sounds of Earth, in case anybody out here wants to know who sent it.

We held the hour. The beacon blinked the whole time.

identity.name: Wembly Voss
identity.story: They are, or were, a terraforming compliance inspector. They faked their own retirement party — cake, speeches, a commemorative plaque they show you with genuine pride — and walked onto your ship the same night. They have inspected forty-one colonies. They wanted to see one begin.
identity.line: I have thirty years of experience and a plaque. I can be useful. The plaque is also available.
identity.join_note: Knows colony regulations from the enforcement side. Insufferable and invaluable at paperwork moments.
